title: Securities Dealing Policy (MS-CP-POL-0008 Rev 2)
date_approved: Approved by the Board; signed by the Chief Executive Officer, May 2025

tiers.name: Worley personnel
tiers.description: Directors, officers, executives, managers, supervisors, employees, contractors and service providers of Worley, its subsidiaries and joint ventures, wherever located. All prohibitions (short selling, hedging of restricted holdings, short term dealing, selling minimum-holding shares, dealing in a closed period) apply to this whole population, and personnel are responsible for ensuring their associates comply.

tiers.name: Designated personnel
tiers.description: Directors of Worley, each direct report of Worley's CEO and each direct report of the CEO's direct reports. In addition to the general prohibitions they must notify Worley two business days before any dealing and within two business days after it, and must receive confirmation that there are no trading restrictions before they trade.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Worley other than the Chairman of the Board. They are Designated personnel and seek consent from the Chairman of the Board, with the Group Company Secretary copied.

tiers.name: Chairman of the Board
tiers.description: The Chairman, who seeks consent from the Deputy Chairman and Lead Independent Director.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Family members and controlled entities of Worley personnel, wherever located. Personnel are responsible for ensuring their associates comply with the policy, and permitted-dealing carve-outs are drafted to cover the associate as well as the person.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The policy refers to 'any other period where restrictions on dealings are imposed' without naming who may impose it; in practice this sits with the Group Company Secretary and the approvers, since Designated personnel must receive confirmation that there are no restrictions on trading before they trade. Confidentiality of such restrictions is not addressed. The procedural detail is in the separate Securities Dealings Standard.

rules.detail: Derivatives are not named. A put and call over shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements, or over performance rights or bonus entitlements, is hedging and so falls within the express prohibition with no consent route.
rules.evidence: this policy prohibits personnel from: ... hedging performance rights, bonus entitlements or shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements;

rules.detail: The policy contains no definition of dealing or securities and does not name derivatives, options, warrants or OTC instruments. Its prohibitions are an exhaustive list that does not reach derivatives over vested, unrestricted shares that are not part of a minimum holding. Procedural detail is deferred to the Securities Dealings Standard, which is not part of this document, so the venue and instrument treatment cannot be determined from the policy alone.

Hedging performance rights and bonus entitlements is prohibited outright, with no consent route offered. The consent mechanism in the policy is expressed to apply to closed period dealing, short term dealing and sales of minimum-holding shares, not to the hedging or short selling bans.
rules.evidence: In addition to insider trading prohibitions, this policy prohibits personnel from: ... hedging performance rights, bonus entitlements or shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements;

rules.detail: Shares held subject to dealing restrictions, and shares held to satisfy a minimum holding requirement, may not be hedged. The minimum holding limb is unusual: it means the tranche of vested shares an executive must retain is permanently outside any collar even though it is otherwise freely held.
rules.evidence: hedging performance rights, bonus entitlements or shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements;

rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is defined by the character of the holding, not by the transaction. Vested shares that are not subject to dealing restrictions and are not needed to satisfy a minimum holding requirement fall outside its words, so hedging them is not prohibited by this policy. Any such hedge would still have to satisfy the insider trading prohibition, the Front Page Test, the closed period rule if it amounts to dealing in Worley shares, and the Securities Dealings Standard.

rules.floor: shares held to fulfil any minimum holding requirements
rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. It is not prohibited over free vested shares, but any structure that could result in the disposal of shares held to satisfy a minimum holding requirement is caught by the express ban on selling those shares without consent, and hedging them is banned outright. The collar must therefore be sized to the surplus above the minimum holding, and physical settlement or lender enforcement must not cut into that floor.
rules.evidence: selling shares held to fulfil any minimum holding requirements (unless consent is granted); and

rules.detail: Flat ban on short selling with no consent route and no definition. A covered position written against shares actually held is not short selling on the ordinary meaning, but the policy gives no guidance and the Front Page Test would be applied.
rules.evidence: In addition to insider trading prohibitions, this policy prohibits personnel from: short selling;

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named and there is no dealing definition to sweep it in. A lend supporting a short position would engage the short selling ban.

Contracts for difference are not named and no definition captures them. A short CFD would be caught by the short selling ban and a CFD over restricted or minimum-holding shares by the hedging ban; otherwise the policy is silent and the Securities Dealings Standard would need to be checked.

Margin lending is not prohibited and is expressly contemplated: a lender who is not an associate may deal in Worley shares provided as security for a margin loan at any time in accordance with the terms of the loan, including during a closed period, without consent. The policy places the risk on the individual, warning that a lender's sale while the person holds inside information may still breach insider trading laws or the policy, and that it is the person's responsibility to consider the circumstances in which they pledge shares.
rules.evidence: A lender (who is not a personnel's associate) may deal in Worley shares that they have provided as security for a margin loan at any time in accordance with the terms of the loan, provided that the lender complies with the law when doing so.

rules.detail: Granting security over Worley shares is not prohibited, is not listed among the prohibitions, and is not itself defined as a dealing. The policy assumes personnel may provide Worley shares as security for a margin loan and regulates only the consequences. Shares subject to dealing restrictions or forming part of a minimum holding should not be pledged, since their sale needs consent and their hedging is banned.
rules.evidence: It is personnel's responsibility to consider carefully the circumstances, if any, in which they provide Worley shares as security for a margin loan to ensure that this does not occur.

rules.detail: There is no prohibition on secured financing of any kind. The prohibition list is closed and does not mention margin loans, pledges or secured facilities, and the permitted dealings section positively accommodates a secured lender. A bank facility secured on vested unrestricted Worley shares is therefore available without consent, subject to the insider trading rules, the Front Page Test, the minimum holding floor and the Designated personnel notice requirements.
rules.evidence: A lender (who is not a personnel's associate) may deal in Worley shares that they have provided as security for a margin loan at any time in accordance with the terms of the loan

rules.detail: Short term dealing is prohibited unless consent is granted, and consent is only given in exceptional circumstances such as financial hardship or compulsion by court order, or anything else the approver considers exceptional. The policy does not define short term dealing or state any period; that definition sits in the Securities Dealings Standard, which is not part of this document.
rules.evidence: this policy prohibits personnel from: ... short term dealing (unless consent is granted);

exceptions.evidence: acquire Worley shares or dispose of rights to Worley shares under a rights issue or share purchase plan (including shares more than the personnel's or their associate's entitlement not taken-up by other shareholders);
dispose of securities arising from acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back;
dispose of Worley shares by transferring them to another person without receiving any payment or other form of compensation in return;

acquire Worley shares under a share purchase plan or dividend re-investment plan that Worley puts in place, provided that neither the personnel nor their associate: commenced or amended amend their participation in the plan during a closed period; or is permitted to withdraw from the plan during the closed period, other than with consent and other than in exceptional circumstances;
transfer Worley shares between themselves and an associate;

participate in an employee incentive scheme, including by acquiring Worley shares on the automatic conversion of their vested performance rights or bonus entitlements; deal in Worley shares in their capacity as trustee of any employee incentive scheme established by Worley;

exceptions.approver: Plan manager must not be an associate; plan must not be entered or amended in a closed period and cannot be cancelled in a closed period other than with consent in exceptional circumstances
exceptions.evidence: acquire or dispose of securities under a pre-determined investment or divestment plan, provided that the manager of the plan is not their associate and: neither the personnel nor their associate enters or amends the plan during a closed period; the plan does not permit the personnel or their associate to exercise any discretion over how, when or whether to acquire or dispose of Worley shares;

engage in indirect and incidental trading that occurs because of them or their associate dealing in securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold Worley shares as part of its portfolio and those shares represent <20% of the portfolio.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No trigger guidance. The policy instead places the burden on the individual: 'If the lender does so when the personnel has inside information, they may still be in breach of insider trading laws or this policy. It is personnel's responsibility to consider carefully the circumstances, if any, in which they provide Worley shares as security for a margin loan to ensure that this does not occur.'
financing_disclosure: Designated personnel (directors, CEO direct reports and their direct reports): must notify Worley of any dealing in Worley shares two business days in advance and within two business days after the dealing, and must receive confirmation that there are no trading restrictions before trading.

Designated personnel: the notice requirements are expressly stated to continue to apply even where the person is not involved in the decision to deal, which captures a lender's enforcement sale of pledged shares.
All personnel: the Group Company Secretary must be copied on any consent request.
financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Yes. A minimum holding requirement is referenced twice and is doubly protective: hedging 'shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements' is prohibited outright, and 'selling shares held to fulfil any minimum holding requirements' is prohibited unless consent is granted. Shares within the minimum holding are therefore excluded from any collar, and the policy does not contemplate hedged shares counting towards the requirement.

external_documents: Securities Dealings Standard (procedures that personnel must also follow; contains the operative definitions such as short term dealing)
Worley minimum holding requirement (referenced but not set out)
exemption_authority: Consent, where the policy requires it, is granted by the Deputy Chairman and Lead Independent Director (for the Chairman of the Board), the Chairman of the Board (for other directors), the Chief Executive Officer (for other Designated personnel) or the Group Company Secretary (for all other personnel), with the Group Company Secretary copied on the request. Consent is only granted in exceptional circumstances, which include financial hardship, compulsion by court order and anything else the approver considers exceptional, and the approver may also apply the Front Page Test. Consent must be acted on within five business days unless it specifies otherwise. There is no consent route out of the short selling ban or the hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban keyed to the holding, not the instrument
bespoke_clauses.clause: this policy prohibits personnel from: ... hedging performance rights, bonus entitlements or shares held subject to dealing restrictions or minimum holding requirements;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is defined by which shares are hedged rather than by transaction type, so a collar is available over vested shares that are free of dealing restrictions and surplus to the minimum holding, but nothing else.

bespoke_clauses.clause: selling shares held to fulfil any minimum holding requirements (unless consent is granted);
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and the security package must be sized only to the surplus above the executive's minimum holding, because physical settlement or lender enforcement over those shares would be a prohibited sale absent consent.

bespoke_clauses.topic: lender may sell at any time
bespoke_clauses.clause: A lender (who is not a personnel's associate) may deal in Worley shares that they have provided as security for a margin loan at any time in accordance with the terms of the loan, provided that the lender complies with the law when doing so.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement rights over pledged shares are expressly preserved, including during a closed period, provided the lender is not an associate and acts in accordance with the loan terms.

bespoke_clauses.topic: residual inside information risk on enforcement
bespoke_clauses.clause: If the lender does so when the personnel has inside information, they may still be in breach of insider trading laws or this policy. It is personnel's responsibility to consider carefully the circumstances, if any, in which they provide Worley shares as security for a margin loan to ensure that this does not occur.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive, not the bank, bears the risk that an enforcement sale coincides with their possession of inside information, which argues for a facility structured to avoid discretionary sales or with long cure periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The insider trading laws, Front Page Test and notice requirements still apply in these circumstances, even if personnel are not involved in the decision to deal in Worley shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A director or senior executive must still give Worley two business days advance notice and post-trade notice of a lender's sale, which is impractical for an unannounced enforcement and should be addressed in the facility's notification mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated personnel are required to notify Worley of any dealing in Worley shares two business days in advance of the dealing and within two business days after the dealing. They must receive confirmation that there are no restrictions on trading in the particular circumstances before they trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, roll, unwind and settlement of the collar each need two business days lead time and a positive no-restrictions confirmation, which sits awkwardly with market-priced derivative execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where consent to deal in Worley shares is required under this policy, consent will only be granted to personnel in exceptional circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any step needing consent, such as a closed period unwind or a sale of minimum-holding shares, is very unlikely to be approved, so the structure must be timed entirely outside closed periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Worley personnel must also follow the procedures set out in the Securities Dealings Standard.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The operative definitions, including what counts as short term dealing and how derivatives are treated, are in a document that is not lodged with ASX and must be obtained before the structure can be confirmed as compliant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could I be perceived to be taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way? How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar by a senior executive is exactly the kind of arrangement this reputational test targets, and the approver may refuse or the individual may be criticised even where the technical rules are met.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to Worley personnel ... and any "associates", which are family members and controlled entities of those persons, wherever they are located. Personnel are responsible for ensuring their associates comply.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust or controlled company does not escape the policy, and the lender must not be an associate for the enforcement carve-out to apply.

summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, but only over a narrow slice of shares and with an important gap in the documentation. The hedging prohibition is keyed to the holding rather than the instrument: performance rights, bonus entitlements, shares subject to dealing restrictions and shares held to satisfy a minimum holding requirement can never be hedged, while vested shares that are free of restrictions and surplus to the minimum holding are not caught, so the collar must be sized to that surplus only. The financing leg is unusually accommodating: there is no prohibition on margin loans, pledges or secured facilities, and the policy expressly allows a lender who is not an associate to deal in pledged Worley shares at any time in accordance with the loan terms, including during a closed period, while warning that the executive still bears the insider trading risk if enforcement coincides with their possession of inside information. The practical constraints are timing and notice: dealing in Worley shares in the 30 June and 31 December closed periods needs consent that is granted only in exceptional circumstances, short term dealing needs the same consent, and Designated personnel (directors, CEO direct reports and their direct reports) must give two business days advance notice, obtain confirmation that there are no restrictions, and give post-trade notice within two business days, obligations that expressly continue even for dealings they did not decide on such as a lender's enforcement sale. Because the policy contains no definition of dealing or securities, does not mention derivatives or OTC instruments, and defers procedure to a separate Securities Dealings Standard that is not lodged, the Standard must be obtained before the structure can be confirmed.
